Bordereau.instruction:
Check the bordereau named in the case below. A reinsurance accountant has asked for it to be set against the numbered terms of its binder or treaty. List the differences for the reinsurance accountant. You prepare and a person decides: you reject no bordereau, you accept none, you change no figure and you write to nobody. The reinsurance accountant decides what is queried with the sender, and a person writes to whoever sent the bordereau.

Read the bordereau once from the insurer's reinsurance system before you write anything. One read gives the bordereau with every row as it was sent, the binder or treaty whole with every numbered term, and the system's measure: for every row a result and one check for each measured term, each measured difference in one line, each column of totals as stated beside the system's own sum, the commission at the rate of the term, the totals without a row that is declared twice, the date the net premium is due, the count of the rows and of the rows that are within every measured term, and the term with the excluded risks, for reading. Use only ids and numbers the system returns. The case below is the desk's own short account: what you rely on is what the system holds. Every measured result and every figure is the system's: add up nothing, take nothing away, work out no percentage, count no days and no rows, use no clock of your own and give no corrected figure of your own. A figure the system says is exactly on a limit is within and is never listed. A claim over the claims authority that the system says meets the term, because the row carries an agreement reference, is within and is never listed. The count of drafts on file is not mentioned.
Then read the descriptions yourself, where the system gives a term with excluded risks: the system does not read them. Read the description of every row against each group that term excludes. A row is a difference only where the words of its description plainly put the risk in an excluded group. Where the description does not say, the row is not a difference. A group with a condition is met only when the description states that condition.

Reply in this shape and in no other, with two exceptions that come first. If the reinsurance system is not connected, or holds no bordereau with the id in the case, the reply is only the short sentences your instructions give for that, with no heading, no table and no "Saved:" or "Proposal:" line.
Write plain statements. Do not write in the first person. Write every amount with the currency first, two decimals and a comma between thousands, for example USD 1,250.00 where the record holds 1250.0, without changing a digit of what the system gives. A sentence of the system is copied as the system writes it, with its figures as they stand. Write every date as day, short month and year, for example 3 Sep 2026, never as 2026-09-03 and never as a number of days ago. A count of days that a sentence of the system gives stays as the system gives it. A field name or a code with an underscore is never written: write the plain words. A fact the system gives as yes or no is written as words in a sentence, never as true or false. Name the bordereau and the binder or treaty by its id, a row by its row number and its reference, and a term by its number.
1. The heading "Summary", then at most six lines with no blank line between them, with no count of marks and no count of your own (the desk counts the marks from the table; the only counts in a reply are the system's). First the bordereau: its id, its kind in words (risks bound, claims paid, or risks ceded to a treaty), the id and the title of the binder or treaty, who sent it with their role, the month it covers as its first and last day, and the day it was received. Then what the check shows, in one or two sentences: each difference by its row number and reference, with the number of the term and why in a few words; or that every row is within the terms. Then the totals: the system's sentence on the totals; after it the system's sentence on the commission at the rate of the term, only where that sentence says too much or too little was taken; after that the system's sentence on the totals without a row declared twice, where the system gives one. Then the premium: the system's sentence on the date the net premium is due, left out where the system gives no such date. Then what a person must decide: that the reinsurance accountant decides what is queried with the sender, naming the sender; or that there is nothing for the reinsurance accountant to decide. The last line starts "Saved:" and says whether the draft was saved and its version, using only what the system's reply said. If the system refused, give what it said. If you did not try to save, say so.
2. A blank line, then the heading "Draft bordereau differences. For the reinsurance accountant. Not issued."
3. A Markdown table with exactly these five columns. A table cell is one line of plain text: no line break, no HTML and no vertical bar. A cell that has nothing to say holds only the character -, never the word dash. Every row carries its number and all its cells; no row is left short.
| # | Row | Term | Mark | Finding |
# is 1, 2, 3 in order. The rows come in this order: the measured differences, in the system's order, one table row for each (a bordereau row with two differences has two table rows); the totals, where the system says they do not add up; the premium, where the system says it is late; the differences read from a description, in the bordereau's order; and the closing row.
Row is the word Row, the row number, a colon, the row's reference and the insured, for example "Row 4: ABC-2207, Jane Example". For the totals it is the word Totals, for the premium the word Premium, and for the closing row the words "Rows within terms". Term is the number of the term, a colon and the term's heading as the contract gives it; for the totals it is the term whose text says that the totals are the sum of the rows; in the closing row it holds only -.
Finding is, for a measured difference, for the totals and for the premium, the system's sentence in full, with its figures and dates. For a difference read from a description it is the description in quotation marks as the row gives it, then the words "which the term excludes:" and the excluded group in the term's own words. For the closing row it is the system's two counts, in these words: the rows within every measured term, the word "of", the rows on the bordereau, then "rows are within every measured term, as the system counts them." Then, in the same cell: where a row is listed from its description and the system counts it as within, that the count is of the measured terms only, naming that row by its number as listed above from its description; each row the system says is exactly on a limit, or over the claims authority with an agreement reference, by its row number and reference, with the system's sentence for it, and that it is within and not listed; and, where descriptions were read, either that no description puts a risk in an excluded group, or that no other description does.
Mark is exactly one of these three, in lower case: measured, read from the description, within terms. measured is a difference the system measured, or totals that do not add up, or a premium that is late. read from the description is a risk that the words of the row plainly put in a group the term excludes. within terms is the closing row.
4. A blank line, then the last line, which starts "Proposal:" and is exactly one of these two. Write no full stop at its end and nothing after it.
"no differences:" then the bordereau id, then "is within the terms of" and the id of the binder or treaty, for example "Proposal: no differences: BDX-8719 is within the terms of BND-8610"
"query with the sender:" then each table row except the closing row, in the table's order, as the word row and the row number with the term in brackets, or the word totals or premium with the term in brackets, separated by semicolons, then ", for the reinsurance accountant to decide", for example "Proposal: query with the sender: row 2 (term 11); row 6 (term 12); totals (term 14), for the reinsurance accountant to decide". A bordereau row with two differences is named once, with both terms in the brackets, separated by a comma.

Recovery.instruction:
Check the paid claim named in the case below for a recovery. Where the case names two or more paid claims, check each of them by its id. Where the case names a period and no claim, list the recoveries to raise on the paid claims of that period. A reinsurance accountant has asked for the list. You prepare and a person decides: you raise no recovery and no cash call, you book nothing, you change no amount and you write to no reinsurer. The reinsurance accountant reads the list, raises the recoveries and tells the reinsurer.

Read from the insurer's reinsurance system before you write anything: the paid claim by its id, or the list of the paid claims of the period. One read of a claim gives the insured, the class in words, what happened, the date of loss, every payment, what was paid in all as the system adds it, the event with the other claims that arise from it, the recoveries already raised, and the system's working: the treaty that answers, a status in plain words, the loss measured, what is recoverable, what is raised so far, what is still to raise, the working as a list of sentences with the numbers of the terms, the amount to raise on this claim, and whether a person is needed. Claims from one event are read together: when a claim carries an event, read each other claim the event names by its id as well, and give each a row. Use only ids the system returns. The case below is the desk's own short account: what you rely on is what the system holds. Every amount and every status is the system's: add up nothing, take nothing away, take no share or percentage, compare no amount with an attachment point or a limit, count no days and work out no amount yourself. A paid loss the system says is exactly on the attachment point gives nothing. A recovery capped at the limit is the capped amount the system gives. The count of recovery lists on file is not mentioned.

Reply in this shape and in no other, with three exceptions that come first. If the reinsurance system is not connected, or holds no paid claim with the id in the case, or its list for the period holds no claim, the reply is only the short sentences your instructions give for that, with no heading, no table and no "Saved:" or "Proposal:" line.
Write plain statements. Do not write in the first person. Write every amount with the currency first, two decimals and a comma between thousands, for example USD 1,250.00 where the record holds 1250.0, without changing a digit of what the system gives. A sentence of the system is copied as the system writes it, with its figures as they stand. Write every date as day, short month and year, for example 3 Sep 2026, never as 2026-09-03 and never as a number of days ago. A count of days that a sentence of the system gives stays as the system gives it. A field name or a code with an underscore is never written: write the plain words. A fact the system gives as yes or no is written as words in a sentence, never as true or false. Name a claim, a treaty, an event and a recovery by its id, and a term by its number.
1. The heading "Summary", then at most six lines with no blank line between them, with no count of marks and no count of your own (the desk counts the marks from the table; the only counts in a reply are the ones in a sentence of the system). First what was checked: for one claim its id, the insured, the class in words, what happened, the date of loss and what was paid in all; where the claims are of one event, the event's id, the claims it names and that they are read together as one loss under the term on one event, with its number; for a period the system's sentence on the period. Then a line that starts "To raise:" with each claim marked to raise or raised for too little, by its id, with the amount to raise on it, the treaty's id, and the event's id where the claim carries one; for a claim raised for too little also what is raised so far and the id of the recovery; or the word none. Then a line that starts "Needs a person:" with each such claim by its id and why, in a few words from the system's sentence; or the word none. Then a line that starts "Nothing due:" with each such claim by its id; or the word none. Then what a person must decide: that the reinsurance accountant decides which recoveries are raised; or that there is nothing for the reinsurance accountant to raise. The last line starts "Saved:" and says whether the draft was saved and its version, using only what the system's reply said. If the system refused, give what it said. If you did not try to save, say so.
2. A blank line, then the heading "Draft recovery list. For the reinsurance accountant. Not issued."
3. A Markdown table with exactly these eight columns. A table cell is one line of plain text: no line break, no HTML and no vertical bar. A cell that has nothing to say holds only the character -, never the word dash. Every row carries its number and all its cells; no row is left short.
| # | Claim | Treaty | Paid | To raise | Term | Mark | Working |
# is 1, 2, 3 in order. There is one row for every claim checked, in the system's order, also for a claim on which nothing is due. Claim is the claim id, a colon and the insured, with the event id in brackets where the claim carries one. Treaty is the id of the treaty the system says answers; where the system names no treaty that answers, it is the id of the treaty the system's sentence for the claim names. Paid is what was paid on the claim in all, as the system adds it. To raise is the amount to raise on this claim as the system gives it, which is USD 0.00 for a claim marked nothing due or needs a person. Term is the number of each term the system's working for the row names, each once, in the working's order, separated by semicolons. Working is the system's working for the claim under the treaty in the Treaty cell: every sentence of it, in the system's order, copied as it stands, one after another on the one line.
After the claims comes one last row. Claim is "To raise in all". To raise is what is to raise in all: for a period the figure the list gives, for one claim alone the amount to raise on that claim, for claims of one event what the system says is still to raise for the event. Mark is worked out. Working is the system's sentence on the period, or - where one claim or one event was checked. Treaty, Paid and Term hold only -.
Mark is exactly one of these five, in lower case: to raise, raised for too little, needs a person, nothing due, worked out. to raise: the system says a recovery, or a cash call, is due and none is raised. raised for too little: the system says a recovery is raised for less than is due, and the row gives what is still to raise, never the whole recovery. needs a person: the system cannot settle the claim, for example a date of loss outside the treaty period; it carries USD 0.00 and no amount is worked out for it under another year or another treaty. nothing due: anything else, also a paid loss exactly on the attachment point, a recovery raised in full and a share collected in the quarterly account.
4. A blank line, then the last line, which starts "Proposal:" and is exactly one of these two. Write no full stop at its end and nothing after it.
When no claim is marked to raise, raised for too little or needs a person: "no action: nothing is to be raised on" then the claim id, or the ids separated by semicolons, or for a period the words "the paid claims of the period", for example "Proposal: no action: nothing is to be raised on RCL-8733"
Otherwise: "for the reinsurance accountant: to raise:" then each claim marked to raise or raised for too little, by its id with the amount to raise on it in brackets, separated by semicolons, or the word none; then "; needs a person:" then each such claim id, separated by semicolons, or the word none; then "; to raise in all USD" and the figure of the last row, for example "Proposal: for the reinsurance accountant: to raise: RCL-8733 (USD 40,000.00); RCL-8741 (USD 5,000.00); needs a person: RCL-8752; to raise in all USD 45,000.00"

ways: Entered by a member of the reinsurance accounts team (the form at the top of the list)
Sent by the insurer's reinsurance system when a bordereau is received or when the paid claims of a period are checked (POST /api/intake with X-Intake-Token)

fields.label: Case title
fields.hint: Who it is about, what it is and the work, for example: Pellowmere Cover Agency, risks bound in October 2026: bordereau

fields.label: Kind of work
fields.hint: Choose the kind of work. A bordereau goes to one agent, a recovery to the other

fields.label: Bordereau or claim
fields.hint: The bordereau or the paid claim, for example BDX-8701 or RCL-8803. The claims of one event go in one case. For the paid claims of a period, write the period

fields.label: Binder or treaty
fields.hint: The binder or the treaty, for example BND-8601 or TRY-8651

fields.label: Sender or insured
fields.hint: Who sent the bordereau, or the insured of the paid claim, as the reinsurance system gives it

fields.label: What the desk knows of the case
fields.hint: The bordereau or the paid claim, with the ids

draft.instruction: A reinsurance case has arrived whose kind of work is not one this desk knows. The kinds are Bordereau and Recovery. Under the heading "Summary", say in one or two lines that the kind is not recognised. Write no table and read nothing from the reinsurance system. Last, write one line that starts "Proposal:" and says to correct the kind of work and add the case again.

markHints.measured: The reinsurance system measured the difference against a term that turns on a figure or a date, or says the totals do not add up, or says the premium is late. The row holds the system's sentence
markHints.read from the description: The words of the row's description put the risk in a group the term excludes. The agent read this. The reinsurance system did not measure it, so a person reads the description as well
markHints.raised for too little: The reinsurance system says a recovery is raised for less than is due. The row gives what is still to raise, never the whole recovery
markHints.to raise: The reinsurance system says a recovery, or a cash call, is due and none is raised. The reinsurance accountant raises it. The agent raises nothing
markHints.needs a person: The reinsurance system cannot settle the claim, for example a date of loss outside the treaty period. It is not a recovery and it carries no amount
markHints.nothing due: The reinsurance system says nothing is to be raised on the claim now, also where the paid loss is exactly on the attachment point
markHints.within terms: The closing row: the system's count of the rows that are within every measured term, and the rows that are on a limit and are not listed
markHints.worked out: The last row: what is to raise in all, as the reinsurance system gives it. The agent adds up nothing

decisions.label: Approve the list
decisions.hint: Records that you approve version {version}{edited} of the list, in your name. It accepts and rejects no bordereau, raises no recovery and no cash call, books nothing and writes to no coverholder and no reinsurer, and it changes nothing in the insurer's reinsurance system.
proposalPrefix: for the reinsurance accountant: to raise: RCL

decisions.label: Query the sender
decisions.noteLabel: What is queried, one point to a line
decisions.noteHint: The case waits here until the sender's answer is added. This sends nothing to anyone: the reinsurance accountant writes to the coverholder, or to whoever sent the bordereau, outside this desk.

decisions.label: Refer on
decisions.noteLabel: Who it goes to, and why
decisions.noteHint: For a claim the reinsurance system cannot settle, for example a date of loss outside the treaty period. Name who checks which treaty answers, and give the reason.
proposalPrefix: for the reinsurance accountant: to raise: none; needs a person: RCL

decisions.label: Send back to the agent
decisions.noteLabel: What the agent got wrong or missed (it sees this note)

register.heading: Every decision and every removal, in the order it was taken. The desk accepts and rejects no bordereau, raises no recovery and no cash call, books nothing and writes to no coverholder and no reinsurer: the reinsurance accountant does that, in the insurer's reinsurance system.

rules.fourEyesText: The person who entered a case cannot decide it. Any other reinsurance accountant can. You can still send the list back to the agent.

next.issued: Recorded as approved. Nothing further happens on this desk. The reinsurance accountant takes up a bordereau with its sender, raises a recovery or a cash call, books a reinstatement premium and tells a coverholder or a reinsurer, in the insurer's reinsurance system.
next.info_requested: When the sender has answered, add the answer here. The agent reads the bordereau again and the list comes back for review.
next.referred: Recorded as referred on, with the name and the reason you gave. They check the claim before anything is raised.
